newsitem.title: USA: US Senators raise concern over rural utility loans.
newsitem.headline: US Senators raise concern over rural utility loans.

text.p: U.S. senators Tuesday raised concern about the federal government's exposure to massive loans to rural electric cooperatives which might turn bad if they cannot survive in a competitive power market.
The Agriculture Department's Rural Utilities Service has $32 billion in outstanding loans to electric cooperatives.
About $8 billion of the total is owed by 12 borrowers who face bankruptcy or are considered likely to default, according to the General Accounting Office.
The Rural Utilities Service has already written off more than $1 billion in bad loans over the last five years.

Service director Wally Beyer said he could not predict how much the agency would be able to recover, but tried to reassure the Senate Agriculture, Nutrition and Forestry Committee that talks with the borrowers were going well.
"We don't at this point feel there's going to be a need for huge write-offs if we can extend some loans," he said.
Senator Rick Santorum urged Beyer to focus on lowering the federal government's exposure at a time when the power industry is becoming competitive across the country.
"The deregulation that is coming ... could dramatically disrupt all of these rural electric cooperatives," Santorum said.

Beyer responded that the agency was encouraging its strong borrowers to turn to private capital markets, but moves to deregulate local power markets would make it increasingly difficult for rural utilities to borrow money.

"Capital is going to flow to where the profit centers are. There are not many profit centers in rural America," he said, adding that supplying power in rural areas would always be more expensive than in industrial and highly-populated areas.

The biggest source of financial stress on past loans was investments in nuclear power plants, he said. Most of the agency's loans are to cooperatives that own distribution facilities rather than those that own generation and transmission facilities.
